resumen: A dumbbell held upright against the chest and a deep squat. The load in front helps keep the torso upright, which is why it is often used to learn to squat well.
ejecucion: Hold a dumbbell upright by one end, with both hands, against your chest.
Feet a little wider than your shoulders, toes slightly turned out.
Squat down between your legs, with your elbows inside your knees and your chest up.
Go down as far as you can keep your back straight and your heels on the floor.
Stand up by pushing the floor away, keeping the dumbbell against your chest.
matices: That the load in front helps keep the torso more upright is the usual reason for teaching it, and the cited review supports it, but few studies have measured it against other variations. In practice, with heavy loads the limit is often holding the dumbbell, not the legs.
